title: Max Consecutive Ones
statement: `nums` contains only `0`s and `1`s. Return the length of the longest unbroken stretch of adjacent `1`s in it, or `0` if it has no `1` at all.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every starting position and counting forward works but repeats work, O(n²) in the worst case. Instead, read the array once and keep the length of the run of `1`s that ends at the current position: a `1` extends it, a `0` breaks it. The answer is the largest value that running length ever reaches.

## Approach

1. Start `best` and `current` at 0.
2. For each `num` in `nums`:
   - if it is `1`, add one to `current` and update `best` if `current` is larger;
   - if it is `0`, the run is broken, so reset `current` to 0.
3. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1]`. The first two `1`s make `current` 1 then 2, and `best` becomes 2. The `0` resets `current` to 0. The last three `1`s raise `current` to 1, 2, 3; at 3 it passes `best`, which becomes 3. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `nums`.
- Space: O(1): two counters.

## Pitfalls

- Update `best` while the run grows (or once more after the loop); updating it only when a `0` appears misses a run that reaches the end of the array.
- An array with no `1` must give `0`, so start `best` at 0.
- Reset `current` to 0, not 1, on a `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | longest run of `1`s seen so far |
| `current` | length of the run of `1`s ending at the current position |
| `num` | the value being read |

narration.2: No run has been seen yet, so the best length starts at 0.
narration.3: current is the length of the run of 1s that ends at the current position.
narration.4: Read the values from left to right.
narration.7: Remember the run if it is the longest so far.
narration.9: A 0 breaks the run; the next 1 starts a new one.
narration.12: best now holds the longest run anywhere in the array.
